text:
Two teams whose seasons are defined off the ice met in Tampa on Saturday. Detroit is playing without its captain, Dylan Larkin, who is suspended after refusing to report until he is traded, and the reports have the Wild and Canadiens circling. Tampa Bay has Nikita Kucherov, who has asked for a trade and, as Daily Faceoff put it, keeps giving the Lightning everything on the ice anyway. On the night, the story was Daniil Tarasov. He stopped all 31 shots, and Detroit won 2-0 to end a five-game winless run.

This was not a game the Red Wings controlled. Tampa had 61 shot attempts to 40, owned the first period (0.98 expected goals to 0.19, the quality of chances), and won this game in 80% of our replays of every shot. Tarasov saved three goals more than those shots usually allow, and by our measure he added more to the win than anyone else on the ice. He stopped John Carlson's 24% look in the first, the best chance of the night, and Jake Guentzel late in the third with the game still 1-0.

Lucas Raymond scored the only goal that mattered at 13:12 of the second, off a William Wallinder feed, moving Detroit's win chance from 48% to 69%. Raymond then set up Michael Brandsegg-Nygård for the clincher with 43 seconds left. Andrei Vasilevskiy was good too, 20 saves on 21, and finished as the second star.

For Todd McLellan's team, which has Moritz Seider talking about leading a room without a captain, this was the kind of result that buys a few calm days, even if the process says it was borrowed. Tampa, still without Brayden Point on injured reserve, had a two-game winning streak end. The Lightning couldn't get anything through on two power plays either.
headline: Tarasov steals one for a Red Wings team under siege
